correctness.rationale: Burnside basis theory gives G/Phi(G)=F_p^2 and generation exactly for independent images, hence the isolate-plus-complete-multipartite decomposition. The two-white analysis completely classifies minimum zero forcing sets, and any three-white state cannot finish. Exact rank-one, rank-two hyperbolic, and rank-three Lorentz witnesses give upper bounds. For part size at least three, any hypothetical rank-two symmetric realization would require each multipartite part to occupy an isotropic line of a nondegenerate two-dimensional form; there are at most two such lines but p+1>=3 parts, proving the lower bound. The packaged verifier exhaustively checks the smallest polynomials and all tested witness patterns and ranks.

value.rationale: The theorem turns the zero forcing polynomial of a canonical finite-group graph into generation data: the minimum coefficient counts unordered generating pairs, and the degree plus next coefficient recover p and the Frattini size. The real minimum-rank phase transition additionally gives an exact criterion for Z=M versus Z=M+1. This is a natural complete structural statement about two-generated p-groups, not a routine single-parameter substitution.
